== Summary ==

On July 7, 2025, Fandom published a blog post detailing its new initiative: using AI to translate English wikis into other languages. The blog can be read here:

[[w:User_blog:Fandom/Introducing Fandom’s Wiki Internationalization Experiment - A Gateway for Editors and Expanding the Fan Experience]]

This move has sparked widespread concern across the community. The list of groups expressing opposition includes:

* Wiki Specialists  
* Global Discussion Mods  
* Volunteer Developers  
* SOAP  
* Fandom Stars  
* Former Wiki Reps  
* Former Wiki Managers  
* Community Central Admins  
* Active Fandom Users  
* Inactive Fandom Users  

== Community Concerns ==

Many users have voiced their objections in the comments section of the announcement blog. One critique is as follows:

 "If you really want to help out international users, give international support instead of removing it like Fandom did with IWRs.  
 ...  
 There are already so many abandoned international wikis; what makes Fandom think users are going to want to join ones created by AI that will undoubtedly be riddled with mistakes?"


These comments also show other concerns about:
* The quality and accuracy of AI-generated translations  
* The lack of human oversight  
* The decision being made without any (actually ''in despite of'') community consultation
* The precedent it could set for future AI use, including on English wikis  

== Call to Action ==

Since Fandom made no announcement about this experiment—despite its platform-wide implications—users are encouraging one another to spread the word directly within their communities.

If you are opposed to the AI translation initiative and other automatic content creation, consider adding your name to the community signature list [[w:User:CincinnatiMountain312/Translation_Signatures|here]].

Your voice matters, please make sure it’s heard.
